text:
inc-bot: Pager triggered: P1 embeddings-latency (svc: embedder-pool). Paging oncall team @maya. Link: https://incidents.redwood/1894567890

maya: oncall here. seeing sustained tail latency on embeddings, p95 ~ 1.8s -> p99 ~ 3.2s for last 10m. customers starting to see timeouts. starting mitigation steps.

tom_k: confirmed, dashboard looks noisy. rolling restart of embedder-worker-34 in progress to drain unhealthy GPUs.

lina: FYI customer reports: batch inference calls from mobile app hitting timeout 10s -> multiple 504s. I pulled request ids, will map to tenants.

ryan: quick check: is autoscaler suppressed? I see no scale up events in last 20m. Could be suppressed by burst window.

maya: good call. I manually triggered scale +2 for embedder-pool. will monitor.

sre-bot: Action logged: manual_scale | service=embedder-pool | delta=+2 | actor=maya | time=2026-03-15T14:05:12Z

maya: initial mitigation helped a bit but tail persists. looks like KV cache evictions spiking around the same times. suspect cache churn -> more compute per request.

lina: digging into eviction logs, found many small keys with TTL 0. running a small script to backfill TTL on popular prefixes.

ryan: For alerting follow-up: current alert is "embeddings_latency_high" firing on p95 > 1.5s for 5m. That was too noisy and also didn't capture p99 spikes. Propose we change to p99 > 2.5s for 3m AND keep p95 > 1.8s as a warning (no page).

maya: +1 to that. Also we should annotate runbook with when to scale vs when to restart workers vs when to adjust cache TTLs. Right now runbook only says "investigate".

lina: I can draft runbook snippet. putting a quick YAML here for review then I'll open a PR:

```yaml
- alert: embeddings_latency_high
  severity: page
  metric: request_latency_p99
  threshold: 2.5s
  window: 3m
  runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embeddings-latency
  owner: eng-oncall
  immediate_actions:
    - scale_embedder_pool: +2
    - check_kv_cache_evictions
    - restart_worker_if_errors
  annotation_template: |
    customers_impacted: {tenants}
    mitigation_notes: {actions_taken}
```

tom_k: looks good. add a step to check autoscaler suppression flag and documented command to force scale.

maya: also add a link to the dashboard and the prom query we use. putting prom expr here: 

```promql
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"embedder\"}[5m])) by (le))
```

ryan: for the alert noise problem: add a suppression window for <4hr after a config/deploy, and a tag 'recent-deploy' so we can avoid paging on known flakey periods. but be careful with customer-impacting pages.

maya: agreed. we'll add suppression but keep pages if error-rate > 0.5% or customer 5xx count > 1 for any tenant.

lina: I'll update runbook and open PR: https://git.redwood/internal/runbooks/pulls/42 with changes. reviewers: @tom_k, @maya.

maya: after action items:
- Lina opens PR with runbook + annotated dashboard links (owner: lina)
- Tom will add autoscaler force-scale command to runbook (owner: tom_k)
- Ryan will create a paging rule change in monitoring (owner: ryan)

sre-bot: Runbook PR created: https://git.redwood/internal/runbooks/pulls/42 | CI: passed | reviewers requested: tom_k, maya

maya: quick customer comms: Lina, can you gather tenant ids and we (support) will send 'investigating' notices?

lina: doing now. I'll paste a short template in thread once list is compiled.

ryan: I'll schedule a short post-incident touchpoint tomorrow 09:30 PST to validate alert behavior and confirm annotations are in place.

maya: thanks everyone. leaving note in runbook: "If p99 > 2.5s for 3m AND customer_5xx > 1: page SRE immediately and follow mitigations." will update runbook once PR merges.

tom_k: small housekeeping: adding dashboard panel for "KV cache evictions/sec" and linking it in the runbook. panel id: d-emb-03.

lina: template for customer message: 

> Hi <tenant>, we're investigating intermittent timeouts for embedding requests. We've scaled capacity and are applying mitigations; we'll update within 30 minutes or when we have root cause.

maya: thread summary for postmortem: 
- Trigger: p95 alert + customer timeouts -> escalated by inc-bot.
- Root cause: cache churn + insufficient pool capacity under burst pattern.
- Immediate mitigations: manual scale (+2), restart of noisy workers, backfill TTL for hot keys.
- Follow-ups: alert tuning (p99 threshold), runbook updates (actions & autoscale force command), dashboard panels, PR 42.

sre-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. All actions recorded.

maya: closing thread for now, will re-open if regressions. thanks. :thumbsup:
